note: Two fresh instantiations per pattern, in domains other than trading. copied_runs counts shared runs of eight or more consecutive content words against the source spans; all zero.

patterns.function: 用一个 while 把两个对立的东西装进同一句，理由也放在同一句
patterns.order: thing A > character A > reason A > while > thing B > character B
examples: Wool keeps a rider warm because it holds air, while nylon stays cool because it sheds water.
Oak lasts outdoors because it resists rot, while pine splits easily because it grows fast.
patterns.appropriate: Setting two options against each other where each needs its reason in the same breath.
patterns.forbidden: Splitting the contrast into two sentences, which loses the mirror.

patterns.function: 目的状语从句在前，第一人称动作在后
patterns.order: In order to > purpose > we > verb
examples: In order to keep the bread from drying out, we wrap each loaf the same morning.
In order to stop the dye from bleeding, we rinse every bolt twice.
patterns.appropriate: Opening a method sentence when the reason for the action matters as much as the action.
patterns.forbidden: Flipping it to 'we act to achieve', which this paper's habit does not do.

patterns.function: 倍数写成从最近对手到最远对手的区间，不写 up to
patterns.order: metric > low multiple > high multiple > times that of
examples: Output runs 1.4-2.1 times that of the other looms.
Mileage runs 1.2-1.8 times that of the other routes.
patterns.appropriate: Beating several baselines where the nearest rival should stay visible.
patterns.forbidden: Writing 'up to 2.1 times', which hides how close the best rival gets.

patterns.function: 同一句里把不变的尾部完整重复，只加粗变化的部分
patterns.order: bold part > repeated tail > bold part > repeated tail
examples: Yield is 1.4 times that of the other looms, waste is 0.6 times that of the other looms, and speed is 1.1 times that of the other looms.
Ridership is 1.3 times that of the other lines, fare revenue is 1.5 times that of the other lines, and complaints are 0.8 times that of the other lines.
patterns.appropriate: Three or more comparisons of the same shape in one sentence.
patterns.forbidden: Shortening the repeated tail to 'that of' after the first one.

patterns.function: 先给 Loose 说法，再用 that is to say 收成可检验的说法
patterns.order: loose name > that is to say > precise name
examples: We need the right mix of crops, that is to say, the acreage given to wheat and to barley.
We need a fair split of the shift, that is to say, the hours each nurse works.
patterns.appropriate: Naming a problem twice, once for the reader and once so it can be checked.
patterns.forbidden: Keeping only the precise version and dropping the loose one.

patterns.function: 先把对方的好处说足，再从同一个好处上转出自己的优势
patterns.order: full credit > however > same virtue but superior
examples: Cast iron holds heat well. Aluminium, however, holds heat equally well but weighs far less.
The paved path drains well. The gravel path, however, drains just as well but costs far less to repair.
patterns.appropriate: Ranking two options while looking even-handed.
patterns.forbidden: Praising the rival for something unrelated to the advantage being claimed.

patterns.function: 用如果允许会让研究失去意义来排除一个选项
patterns.order: if allowed > beats everything > study meaningless > so excluded
examples: If riders could transfer without limit, no route plan would matter, so transfers are capped.
If every sample could be retested forever, no protocol would matter, so each sample is tested once.
patterns.appropriate: Dropping an option because allowing it would make the whole study pointless.
patterns.forbidden: Using it for an option that is merely inconvenient rather than fatal to the study.

patterns.function: 先给一般定义，再用 Especially 收成手里这个特例
patterns.order: general definition > Especially > the case in hand
examples: A route is delayed when it runs behind its timetable. Especially, when both the trunk and the feeder run behind, the connection fails.
A batch is sound when every item passes. Especially, when both the cap and the seal pass, the jar ships.
patterns.appropriate: Moving from a textbook definition to the exact case the data supports.
patterns.forbidden: Using Especially for a case the data does not actually contain.

patterns.function: 稳定性写成 only when 加一个闭区间
patterns.order: stable only when > parameter in [low, high]
examples: The oven holds its crust only when the temperature stays inside 180 to 200 degrees.
The dye takes evenly only when the bath stays inside 40 to 55 degrees.
patterns.appropriate: A parameter that behaves well only inside a bounded window.
patterns.forbidden: Reporting the window without saying what fails on each side.

patterns.function: 区间两侧各给一个失败原因，用 while 连
patterns.order: too short > failure > while > too long > failure
examples: Too short a proof and the dough collapses, while too long a proof and the dough sours.
Too short a soak and the stain holds, while too long a soak and the fabric weakens.
patterns.appropriate: Both ends of a range fail, and for different reasons.
patterns.forbidden: Giving a reason for only one side.

patterns.function: 拒绝一个方法时给态度：Out of caution, we do not choose
patterns.order: risky option > Out of caution > rejected > plain alternative
examples: Out of caution, we do not choose the untested varnish, but use the one the shop already trusts.
Out of caution, we do not choose the new roster, but keep the rotation the ward already knows.
patterns.appropriate: Declining a fashionable method for a reader who expects it.
patterns.forbidden: Rejecting the method without naming the plain alternative.

patterns.function: 给一个行业常识阈值来给自己的数定位
patterns.order: our value > Usually near threshold indicates > so ours qualifies
examples: Our line runs at 92 percent. Usually a line near 90 percent is counted as full, so ours qualifies.
Our ward turns beds over in 48 minutes. Usually a ward near 45 minutes is counted as quick, so ours qualifies.
patterns.appropriate: Placing one's own number against a rule of thumb the reader already knows.
patterns.forbidden: Inventing a threshold the field does not actually use.
